newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Overnight break announced in Russia-NATO talks.
newsitem.headline: Overnight break announced in Russia-NATO talks.

text.p: Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and NATO Secretary General Javier Solana took a break until Wednesday morning after a day of talks on future relations between Russia and the Western alliance, a Western source said.

Solana could be seen about one a.m. on Wednesday (2100 GMT on Tuesday) getting into his car and driving away from the Foreign Ministry mansion in central Moscow, where he held talks with Primakov. Primakov followed him later.

The source close to talks, who refused to be identified, said the two officials will use the break to have a rest and to hold consultations with their teams to resume talks in the morning. He could not say when the talks would restart.
Officials were not immediately available for comments.
Russia, worried by NATO's plans to grant membership to some eastern European countries, is negotiating a special deal which could meet some of its security concerns.

Russian President Boris Yeltsin has said he wanted to sign the deal in Paris on May 27. But Primakov indicated on Tuesday that the fate of the document strongly depended on how strongly NATO was ready to compromise.
Moscow wants a say in NATO decisions and strong guarantees that the alliance would not move its troops and nuclear weapons to the territories of the new members.
NATO says it has no such plans but appears reluctant to give any guarantees for the future, arguing that it cannot make any commitments which could affect rights of the new members.
